subject: Post-call recap: Cost/TCO discussion with NovaCorp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap: Cost/TCO discussion with NovaCorp

Hi Jordan / Alyssa - thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps so we can build a targeted 6-month TCO and ROI view.

Key pain points you shared:
- Token cost volatility with current provider is driving unexpected overages during peak runs (marketing campaign spikes).
- Need predictable monthly spend (finance target ~$30k/mo) while improving model accuracy for customer-facing flows.
- Latency spikes at peak concurrency affecting user experience (p95 target <= 200ms).

Goals we discussed:
1) Reduce per-inference unit cost by ~30-40% without regressing quality.
2) Achieve p95 latency <= 200ms on production traffic.
3) Put a clear 6-month ROI plan in front of finance for approval.

Cost levers and quick feasibility notes (these will go into the TCO workbook):
- Model choice + quantization: moving to an 8-bit quantized variant can reduce GPU token cost by ~20-35% depending on accuracy tradeoffs.
- Batching and continuous batching: for conversational flows (avg token length ~80), batching can cut per-token inference cost significantly during sustained throughput.
- Prefix/KV caching: for repeated prompts (user profile + template), hit rates can meaningfully lower tokens sent to the model and reduce latency.
- Smart routing: route low-priority or offline jobs to lower-cost model variants or scheduled batch windows.
- Dedicated vs hosted tiers: Dedicated capacity gives predictable throughput and often a better unit price at commit; hosted is faster to start.

Ask from you so we can finalize the workbook and ROI scenarios:
- Average API calls/day (or calls/week) for the two priority flows we discussed.
- Avg and 95th token length per call (if available).
- Current monthly spend on model inference (approx).
- Any hard constraints from finance on multi-month commit or vendor terms.

Attachments: nova_tco_estimate.xlsx (initial workbook we discussed), redwood_pricing_summary.pdf (pricing bands / dedicated commit options).

Proposed next steps:
1) You share the traffic and token metrics above by end of week (Fri 2026-04-24).
2) Rafael and I will build 3 scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive) and circulate the 6-month TCO workbook by Tue 2026-04-28.
3) Schedule a 45-min follow-up next week to walk through numbers + decision points (Rafael to join on the infrastructure and dedicated capacity side).

If that plan looks good, I'll schedule time. Thanks again - big opportunity to lock predictable economics without sacrificing quality.

Best,

Great questions - quick answers and next steps below.

1) Caching and multi-tenant safety:
- Prefix / KV caching is tenant-aware: keys are namespaced per-customer and per-user by default, so there is no cross-tenant leakage. We can show an implementation example and the namespace pattern (hashed tenant_id + prompt_signature) in the workbook.

2) Latency SLOs:
- Hosted tier: we publish median and p95 latency benchmarks in the pricing summary and the hosted SLA (p95 best-effort; subject to shared noisy neighbors).
- Dedicated: SLA-backed p95 targets are available with reserved capacity and can be part of the committed package we propose. Rafael will scope expected p95 targets given your concurrency profile.

3) ROI scenario we'll model (per your ask):
- Scenario A: 30% reduction in variable token cost + 50% reduction in scheduled batch window costs.
- Scenario B: conservative (15% variable reduction)
- Scenario C: aggressive (40% variable reduction + dedicated commit discount).

Next steps / timeline:
- Jordan/Alyssa: please send the traffic and token metrics Jordan shared into this thread (if you can attach a CSV or confirm the numbers above) by EOD Fri 2026-04-24.
- Rafael and I will produce the 6-month workbook and a short slide summary. Deliverable target: Tue 2026-04-28 morning PT.
- Proposed follow-up: Thu 2026-04-23 1:30-2:15pm PT (Jordan suggested Thurs afternoon) - I can schedule; Rafael will join to cover dedicated capacity and expected latency.
